key_insight: LLM-generated rubrics can approximate human-made paper-reproduction rubrics, but only when generation is augmented; otherwise they tend to be too fine-grained and score-inflated.
engineering_relevance: For research agents and benchmark builders, checklist-style rubric generation could reduce expert annotation cost while still enabling scalable, paper-specific reproduction evaluation.
method: Reformulated paper-specific rubrics into a checklist-style format.
Compared four rubric-generation settings using two backbone LLMs.
Meta-evaluated rubrics both intrinsically via semantic similarity and extrinsically via alignment with ground-truth rubric scores.
evidence_signal: Across the abstract’s reported experiments, augmented generation settings improved score alignment substantially, with the strongest setting approaching the human baseline.
watch_item: LLM-generated rubrics may be biased toward high scores and less adaptable across paper domains, so they still need human review for high-stakes evaluation.
paper_title: Can LLMs Write Reliable Rubrics? A Meta-Evaluation for Experiment Reproduction
